title: UNIT 6: MECHANICAL OSCILLATION AND SOUND WAVE
notes:
✓ Mechanical oscillation → Repeated to-and-fro motion of an object about an equilibrium position.

✓ Sound → Mechanical wave produced by vibrating objects and transmitted through a material medium.

title: 6.1 COMMON CHARACTERISTICS OF WAVES
notes:
✓ Wave → Disturbance that propagates through space or matter and transfers energy.

✓ Period (T) → Time required for one complete cycle.

✓ Frequency (f) → Number of complete waves passing a point per second.
✓ Unit → Hertz (Hz).

✓ Wavelength (λ) → Distance between identical points on consecutive waves, such as two adjacent crests or troughs.

✓ Amplitude (A) → Maximum displacement from the equilibrium position.

✓ Wave speed (v) → Distance travelled by a wave per unit time.

◆ IMPORTANT RELATIONSHIPS
✓ f = 1/T
✓ T = 1/f
✓ v = fλ

title: 6.1.1 PARTS OF A WAVE
notes:
◆ PARTS OF A WAVE
✓ Crest → Highest point of a transverse wave.
✓ Trough → Lowest point of a transverse wave.
✓ Equilibrium position → Undisturbed position of particles.
✓ Amplitude → Maximum displacement from equilibrium.
✓ Wavelength → Distance between successive corresponding points.

✓ Greater amplitude → More energy is carried by the wave.

title: 6.2 STRING, PENDULUM AND SPRING
notes:
✓ Pulse → Single traveling disturbance.

✓ Wave → Series or train of pulses traveling through a medium.

✓ Periodic motion → Repeated to-and-fro motion that occurs at regular time intervals.

✓ Examples → Swinging pendulum, vibrating spring, ticking clock and heartbeat.

title: 6.2.1 SIMPLE PENDULUM
notes:
✓ Simple pendulum → Consists of a small bob suspended from a light, inextensible string.

✓ Simple pendulum → When displaced from equilibrium, it swings back and forth periodically.

◆ PERIOD OF A SIMPLE PENDULUM
T = 2π√(L/g)

✓ L → Length of pendulum.
✓ g → Acceleration due to gravity.

✓ Period → Depends on length and g, but not on the mass of the bob.

✓ Pendulum → Can be used to determine the acceleration due to gravity.

title: 6.2.2 SPRING AND HOOKE'S LAW
notes:
✓ Spring → Produces a restoring force that acts toward the equilibrium position.

✓ Hooke's Law → Restoring force is directly proportional to displacement from equilibrium.

Fᵣₑₛ = −kx

✓ k → Spring constant/stiffness.
✓ x → Displacement.
✓ Unit of k → N/m.

✓ Negative sign → Shows that the restoring force acts opposite to displacement.

◆ APPLIED FORCE
Fₐₚₚ = kx

title: 6.2.3 SPRING-MASS OSCILLATION
notes:
✓ Spring-mass system → A mass attached to a spring oscillates periodically about its equilibrium position.

◆ PERIOD
T = 2π√(m/k)

✓ m → Mass.
✓ k → Spring constant.

✓ Period → Depends on the mass and stiffness of the spring.

title: 6.3 PROPAGATION OF WAVES AND ENERGY TRANSMISSION
notes:
✓ Wave propagation → Movement of a disturbance from one place to another while transferring energy.

✓ Waves → Are classified according to whether they require a medium and according to the direction of particle vibration.

title: 6.3.1 MECHANICAL WAVES
notes:
✓ Mechanical waves → Require a material medium for propagation.

✓ Mechanical waves → Travel through vibrations of particles in the medium.

✓ Examples → Sound waves, water waves and waves on strings.

✓ Mechanical waves → Cannot travel through a vacuum.

title: 6.3.2 ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES
notes:
✓ Electromagnetic waves → Consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields and do not require a material medium.

✓ Examples → Light, radio waves and X-rays.

✓ Electromagnetic waves → Can travel through a vacuum.

title: 6.3.3 TRANSVERSE AND LONGITUDINAL WAVES
notes:
◆ TRANSVERSE WAVE
✓ Transverse wave → Particle vibration is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
✓ Examples → Waves on strings and electromagnetic waves.

◆ LONGITUDINAL WAVE
✓ Longitudinal wave → Particle vibration is parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
✓ Examples → Sound and pressure waves.

◆ PARTS OF A LONGITUDINAL WAVE
✓ Compression → Particles are close together.
✓ Rarefaction → Particles are spread apart.

title: 6.4 SOUND WAVES
notes:
✓ Sound → Mechanical longitudinal wave produced by vibrating objects.

✓ Sound source → Every source of sound is in a state of vibration.

✓ Sound → Requires a material medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.

✓ Sound → Carries energy as it propagates.

title: 6.4.1 PRODUCTION AND PROPAGATION OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Sound → Is produced when an object vibrates.

✓ Vibration → Causes particles of the surrounding medium to vibrate, producing successive compressions and rarefactions.

✓ Sound → Can travel through solids, liquids and gases.

✓ Speed of sound → Solids > liquids > gases.

title: 6.4.2 SPEED OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Speed of sound → Depends on the properties of the medium.

◆ IN AIR AT 0°C
v ≈ 331 m/s

◆ AT TEMPERATURE Tᶜ IN CELSIUS
v = 331√(1 + Tᶜ/273)

✓ Sound → Generally travels faster in warmer air.

✓ Solids and liquids → Speed depends mainly on the structure and properties of the material.

title: 6.4.3 REFLECTION OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Reflection → Bouncing back of sound when it strikes a surface.

✓ Echo → Reflected sound heard separately from the original sound.

✓ Hard surfaces → Such as walls, rocks, metals and buildings are good reflectors.

✓ Soft materials → Such as cloth and wool absorb much of the sound energy.

✓ SONAR → Uses reflected sound to determine distances and sea depth.

title: 6.4.4 REFRACTION OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Refraction → Bending or change in direction of sound caused by changes in its speed.

✓ Refraction of sound → Can occur when sound travels through air layers having different temperatures.

✓ Day → Warmer air near the ground can make sound bend away from the ground.

✓ Night → Cooler air near the ground can make sound bend toward the ground.

title: 6.4.5 DIFFRACTION OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Diffraction → Bending or spreading of sound as it passes through an opening or around an obstacle.

✓ Longer-wavelength sounds → Diffract more strongly.

✓ Low-frequency sounds → Can bend around obstacles more effectively than high-frequency sounds.

title: 6.4.6 INTERFERENCE OF SOUND
notes:
✓ Interference → Occurs when two or more sound waves meet and combine.

◆ TYPES OF INTERFERENCE
✓ Constructive interference → Waves reinforce each other, producing greater amplitude.

✓ Destructive interference → Waves reduce or cancel each other, producing smaller amplitude or silence.

title: 6.5 SUPERPOSITION OF WAVES
notes:
✓ Superposition principle → When two or more waves pass through the same point simultaneously, the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of their individual displacements.

✓ Interference → Is a result of superposition.

◆ TYPES OF INTERFERENCE
✓ Constructive interference → Waves are in phase and amplitude increases.
✓ Destructive interference → Waves are out of phase and amplitude decreases.

title: 6.5.1 STANDING WAVES
notes:
✓ Standing wave → Formed when two identical waves travel in opposite directions in the same medium and superpose.

◆ IMPORTANT POINTS
✓ Node → Point of zero displacement.
✓ Antinode → Point of maximum displacement.

◆ DISTANCES
✓ Adjacent nodes → λ/2.
✓ Adjacent antinodes → λ/2.
✓ Node to adjacent antinode → λ/4.

✓ Examples → Vibrating guitar strings and air columns in musical instruments.

title: 6.6 CHARACTERISTICS OF SOUND WAVES
notes:
✓ Main characteristics of sound → Pitch, loudness and timbre (quality).

◆ PITCH
✓ Pitch → Depends on frequency.
✓ Higher frequency → Higher pitch.
✓ Lower frequency → Lower pitch.

◆ LOUDNESS
✓ Loudness → Depends on amplitude.
✓ Greater amplitude → Louder sound.
✓ Unit → Decibel (dB).

◆ TIMBRE / QUALITY
✓ Timbre → Distinguishes sounds having the same pitch and intensity but produced by different sources.

title: 6.6.1 SOUND POLLUTION
notes:
✓ Sound pollution → Exposure to excessive sound that can cause harmful effects to humans or other organisms.

◆ POSSIBLE EFFECTS
✓ Hearing loss.
✓ Hypertension.
✓ Sleep disturbance.

✓ Sound above about 75 dB → Can become harmful.
✓ Sound above 120 dB → Can be painful.

title: UNIT 6 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ WAVE
✓ Wave → Disturbance that transfers energy.

✓ f = 1/T
✓ v = fλ

◆ PENDULUM
✓ T = 2π√(L/g)

◆ SPRING
✓ Fᵣₑₛ = −kx
✓ T = 2π√(m/k)

◆ TYPES OF WAVES
✓ Mechanical waves → Need a medium.
✓ Electromagnetic waves → Do not need a medium.
✓ Transverse waves → Vibration ⟂ propagation.
✓ Longitudinal waves → Vibration ∥ propagation.

◆ SOUND
✓ Sound → Mechanical + longitudinal wave; cannot travel through a vacuum.
✓ Sound speed → Solids > liquids > gases.

◆ SOUND PHENOMENA
✓ Reflection.
✓ Refraction.
✓ Diffraction.
✓ Interference.

◆ STANDING WAVE
✓ Standing wave → Two identical waves travelling in opposite directions.
✓ Node → Zero displacement.
✓ Antinode → Maximum displacement.

◆ CHARACTERISTICS OF SOUND
✓ Pitch → Frequency.
✓ Loudness → Amplitude.
✓ Timbre → Quality of sound.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Frequency → Tells how often a wave oscillates.
✓ Amplitude → Tells how large the oscillation is.
✓ Wavelength → Tells the distance between corresponding points.
✓ Wave speed → Tells how fast the disturbance travels.
